text:
nora: Heads-up — seeing repeated latency spikes from eu-west dedicated pool since ~09:10 UTC. Spikes line up with these 'impulse' queue backpressure events where hundreds of tiny allocs land at once. NIC and GPU health look fine on the rack side. Anyone else observing the same?
sam: Yep saw the same at 09:13. Dashboard: https://dash.internal/reports/impulse-euwest (p95 jump ~450ms).
nora: Pasted a short snippet from the proxy logs where queue depth jumps:
```
[09:13:02] queue_len=2 -> 18 -> 120 (15s)
[09:13:03] alloc.new tenant=acme-corp size=0.4GB small-batch
[09:13:05] alloc.new tenant=acme-corp size=0.3GB small-batch
[09:13:07] shadow_evict tenant=acme-corp reason=kv-warmup
```
jin: Looks like KV cache regen + client cold-starts => lots of tiny batches. That pattern creates a tight arrival impulse that overwhelms the continuous-batching heuristics.
jin: Short-term mitigation: token-bucket per-tenant admission on the proxy (throttle bursts) + increase prefix cache TTL for heavy tenants.
ops-bot: deploy notice: canary rollout "impulse-queue-throttle" started in eu-west at 09:40 UTC by platform-team (canary size 3 hosts).
elena: Cost note: those tiny allocs are extra scheduling churn; we bill per-alloc unit so an impulse sequence can add ~12% to short-term tokenized cost for the tenant and increase platform usage. Need to be mindful if we put any flat-rate prewarm.
devon: Can we tag noisy tenants with a temporary QoS label and route them to a prewarm pool instead of throttling? Example: `rls tag set acme-corp qoslvl=prewarm` — needs platform approval but cheaper than full dedicated carveout.
kevin: NIC telemetry shows small egress spikes on rack 14 that match the queue windows. Could be tail drop from switch buffer pressure too. I can run a targeted eBPF policer to confirm.
nora: Good point. If it's switch buffer we need to add gentle nic-shaping on the host as a stopgap. Who can own the orchestration this morning?
sam: I can own the mitigations and coordinate with platform to expand canary if ops-bot shows green. Plan: 1) enable token-bucket throttle for impulse bursts (10s window) 2) add temporary qoslvl tag for top 3 tenants by burst rate 3) add impulse_queue_p95 metric to the per-pool dashboard.
jin: +1. I'll push the TTL tweak for kv-prefix to cut warmup. Also will add a small synthetic test to the smoke suite that simulates impulse arrivals.
elena: If Sam is owning, please post a quick runbook snippet here when you start. Also cc infra-costs for visibility. :thumbsup:
sam: Will do — starting now, will update thread with runbook steps and canary results.
